quote: to making the investment. We already have 11 panels.
stewart_read: Customer discloses an existing 11-panel system mid-call, which should trigger Ion's orphaned_flow line of questions (own vs. lease, install company, system size, is it working). The rep never runs any of these; he only asks about the current monthly bill.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged the call unsalvageable and reactively wrapped it up rather than deliberately skipping the orphaned flow, which is the reactive read this entry adopts given no evidence of a considered pivot.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to always run the orphaned_flow qualifiers the moment an existing system is disclosed -- ownership type and install company determine whether this is a hard DQ or a live expansion/battery lead.

quote: Okay. But that's because we got a swimming pool and a spa.
stewart_read: The customer volunteers that his higher bill is driven by a pool and spa -- exactly the kind of higher-load enthusiasm signal that could justify an expansion sale (additional panels or battery) rather than a flat DQ. This is a different revenue angle than the orphaned-system DQ question: it's an upsell opening, not a qualification gate.
coaching_implication: This detail was filed and never returned to. The rep could have asked how many panels the pool/spa load might require, or flagged it for a specialist estimate on system expansion -- instead the rep let it pass silently into the following DQ-flavored exchange.

quote: and that's where I found your phone number.
stewart_read: Customer explains he was searching for New Mexico's tax credit info and that's how Ion got his number -- this is useful context (motivation was tax-credit driven, not bill-pain driven) that the rep never probes further (e.g., did he get a design/quote from anyone else when he had 11 panels installed).
coaching_implication: A quick follow-up ('who installed your original 11 panels, and are you happy with them?') would have surfaced competitive intel and clarified whether this is a real DQ or a live expansion opportunity.

quote: Oh, okay. Yeah. I hear you. Yeah. No. Unfortunately, those have been expired since, like, I believe, the first of the year.
stewart_read: The rep confirms the tax credit is expired, which is accurate per schema's tax_credit_disclosure note about purchased systems, but he delivers it flatly and removes the customer's own reason for even considering expansion without offering the schema's stated alternative purchase-without-tax-credit option.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as simple honesty (schema_compliant), but the missed follow-up -- not mentioning purchase options without the tax credit -- means the rep answered accurately but incompletely.
coaching_implication: When confirming the tax credit is unavailable, pair it with the schema's fallback line about purchase options without the tax credit so the door isn't fully closed on the same breath.

stewart_read: The customer builds a full cost/ROI objection (tax credit gone, twenty-year payback, doesn't make financial sense) and the rep never attempts any reframe -- he simply agrees and exits. Note: the schema's coaching_philosophy.objection_inversion trigger table (documented flips for 'can't afford it' / 'too expensive' / 'not interested') doesn't explicitly cover a payback-period objection from an existing owner considering expansion, so this is an extrapolation beyond the documented flips rather than a clean-cut miss against a scripted trigger.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged this a genuine, well-reasoned financial objection from an informed customer not worth contesting -- a defensible reactive choice, though the schema's multi_angle_resilience principle would still expect at least one attempt before conceding.
coaching_implication: This is a gap worth raising with Kenny directly: Ion's schema has no documented flip for an existing-owner ROI/payback objection. Flag for schema expansion rather than coaching the rep against a script that doesn't exist yet -- do not invent a dollar-figure rebuttal not grounded in this call.

quote: Okay. No. I hear you. Well, I mean, if anything changes, if you if you're ever open to looking into an estimate, I mean, you know where to call.
stewart_read: The call ends with a fully passive door-open ('you know where to call') rather than any rep-owned next step -- no follow-up call scheduled, no offer to have a specialist review the expansion math given the pool/spa load.
coaching_implication: Even on a likely DQ, the rep could have offered one concrete next step (e.g., 'I can have someone run the numbers on adding a few panels for the pool load, no obligation') instead of leaving it entirely on the customer to reinitiate.
